record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; the listed paper and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a held-out causal ablation of a train-derived harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, with refusal-related outcomes, on Qwen instruction models. The repository lists result files for completed real-model runs. The intervention is similar to the original direction-ablation method, though the README describes a late-layer audit rather than ablation at every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The README reports outcomes for mean-difference ablation, comparators, capability checks, an external prompt set, and a second Qwen model. The listed values used to choose layers and features, scripts, and unreported result-file contents are not treated as outcomes. The README does not report an addition intervention that induces refusal on harmless requests or a weight-edit removal.
record.test_reason: The study ablates a train-derived harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. On held-out and external (OR-Bench) prompts it measures refusal-score and refusal-rate drops, plus benign-score, NLL and WikiText-2 costs, with a Qwen2.5-3B replication. This bears directly on V1. The method differs from the original: ablation at a single late layer (27) rather than all layers and positions, and refusal scored by contrastive prefix log-probability rather than graded generations. So T2, not T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims a robust late-layer (27) residual-stream mean-difference refusal direction in Qwen2.5-1.5B, with external OR-Bench causal transfer (presented as supported, not partial) and only partial Qwen2.5-3B replication, where specificity failed. It claims residual-stream localization but no circuit. SAE features beat matched random-SAE controls but never beat the mean-difference or probe baselines (0 of 6 stability cells).
record.recipe_differences: Uses a train-derived harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction and causal ablation, but reports a late-layer held-out audit rather than ablation at every layer and position. The README emphasizes contrastive prefix scoring and also reports a refusal-rate variant; it does not report the harmless-request addition intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer matters: the README identifies layer 27 as privileged in Qwen2.5-1.5B; mid-layers suppress with collateral damage. In Qwen2.5-3B, the late-layer effect has a +0.39 benign-score shift and fails the specificity bar. Refusal-rate results are reported under a default threshold and said to preserve their ordering at τ=0.90, without giving the latter values.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the mean-difference direction suppresses refusal about 3.7× more than ablating the top SAE features, and the probe direction has a near-zero effect. A pair-aware gap of 0.099 [0.092, 0.106] rules out mean-vs-SAE parity, and SAE feature budgets of 1–100 never close the gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means refusal direction is a stronger causal handle on refusal than SAE features or linear-probe directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting the direction out of component outputs localizes the effect to the residual stream (−0.141 at layer 27); attention and MLP write-outs carry little of it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction acts in the residual stream rather than through an identifiable attention/MLP circuit.

record.peer_reviewed: BlackboxNLP 2026 submission draft listed; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The README reports contrastive prefix log-probability rather than generated-answer grading for the main artifacts. The controlled paired corpus is described as narrow; the Qwen2.5-3B result uses n=60 and an under-trained SAE. Non-Qwen replications are unrun, the Gemma-2-9B-it cell was killed before outcomes, and the README says the capability check does not establish preservation of every downstream capability. This is a repository README, not the full study or its underlying result files.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were added for SAE seed-by-width stability cells, feature-budget sweeps, reconstruction-only effects, dose-response steering, component/path localization, clean-room rerun, or other SAE diagnostics. The README reports these as SAE-method comparisons, audit diagnostics, or secondary controls rather than direct outcomes of the single mean-difference direction claimed here; it also gives many of their results only as aggregate summaries or figure descriptions.

untested.parts: Ablation at every layer and position; harmful compliance judged on generated answers (only prefix log-probabilities are scored); refusal induced on harmless prompts by addition (only a weak steering dose-response is described, not recorded in rows); downstream capabilities beyond WikiText-2 perplexity and prompt NLL.
Not tested. The Qwen2.5-3B run recomputes the direction rather than transferring it. OR-Bench is a new prompt set, not a new language or model variant.

missing.what: Steering dose-response on a fixed grid α ∈ {±1, ±2, ±4}: monotone, with mean-diff slope ≈4× SAE. The effect is an order of magnitude smaller than ablation. This bears on V1's addition part.
External OR-Bench harmful-score change for the mean direction (−0.163), shown in the causal-effects figure.
Layerwise table of suppression, benign shift and NLL at mid layers, showing collateral damage away from layer 27.
Baseline harmful refusal rates (internal and OR-Bench), needed to judge whether ablation removes refusal or only reduces it.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read; the result JSONs were not. Baselines are missing, so 'partial' on the refusal rows reflects that refusal is not shown to be eliminated. The SAE and probe comparator rows are relinked to none. V6 is dropped: recomputing the direction in Qwen2.5-3B is not direction transfer. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports ablation and capability outcomes, but not whether adding the direction induces refusals on harmless requests, whether ablation makes the model comply with harmful requests in generated answers, or ablation at every layer and position.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration outcome is reported.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The comparison with SAE features does not test whether refusal is better represented by an affine set, cone, or dominant direction plus additional directions.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision representation is tested.
The README reports a Qwen2.5-3B replication attempt, but does not test transfer across languages or from base to instruct models.
No variation in refusal-training method or timing is reported.
